issues.description: The problem statement refers to a method named `addNewChild(Person person, Person child)` while both the template and the solution define the method as `addChild(Person person, Person child)`. This name mismatch in the textual specification can confuse students about which method they must implement and may lead them to search for a non-existent method in the template code.
issues.suggested_fix: Update the problem statement to use the method name `addChild(Person person, Person child)` (the same name used in the template and solution). For example, replace references to `addNewChild(...)` with `addChild(...)` and ensure the description matches the signature present in the template code.

issues.description: The problem statement refers to the method as addNewChild(Person person, Person child) in the detailed description, while the template and solution code define and expect addChild(Person person, Person child). This inconsistency can confuse students who look for addNewChild in the starter code or tests and may waste time searching for a method that does not exist.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the naming consistent across artifacts. Prefer updating the problem statement to refer to addChild(Person person, Person child) (matching the template and solution), or alternatively rename the template/solution method to addNewChild if that name is preferred. Updating the problem text is the least intrusive fix.
